quiz.q: According to John Burton's cobweb model, how has the nature of world politics fundamentally changed?
options: Cross-border social ties show that sovereign states are no longer the only gateways of interaction.
States act like impenetrable colliding balls, determining world politics solely through competitive military alliances.
Global institutions have completely replaced nation-states as the primary sovereign actors in world affairs.
Political leaders exclusively regulate international cooperation by directing all formal Track 1 diplomatic negotiations.
quiz.why: John Burton argued that the world is society-centric, meaning states are no longer the sole gateway for cross-border interactions.

quiz.q: How does Ernst Haas's neo-functionalism fundamentally modify David Mitrany's classical functionalist approach to regional integration?
options: It insists that political leaders must be excluded entirely so technical experts can direct integration.
It asserts that sustained integration eventually stalls unless political leaders actively provide necessary political will.
It argues that military alliances must precede economic integration to deter external security threats.
It requires all participating nations to adopt republican constitutions before beginning low-politics technical cooperation.
quiz.why: Ernst Haas argued that functional integration stagnates without the active involvement and political will of political leaders.

quiz.q: According to Michael Doyle, why do democratic nations tend not to go to war with one another?
options: Technocratic agencies gradually replace national parliaments, eliminating political rivalries through shared economic integration.
Democratic governments maintain superior military arsenals that mutually deter any potential aggressive foreign attacks.
Democratic norms, public opinion, and institutional checks create mutual tolerance and opportunities for course correction.
Bilateral trade treaties legally prohibit democratic executives from mobilizing armed forces against commercial partners.
quiz.why: Doyle explains that democracies form a zone of peace due to domestic public pressure, free speech, and mutual tolerance.

quiz.q: What is considered the most serious criticism of how democratic peace theory has been applied in practice?
options: It discourages multilateral global institutions from mediating border disputes between non-democratic sovereign regimes.
It mistakenly assumes that technical experts can easily resolve high-politics territorial conflicts without politicians.
It underestimates the role of trans-national communication and student exchange programs in reducing mistrust.
It has been used to justify military intervention and armed regime change under the Bush Doctrine.
quiz.why: Critics argue the theory provided ideological legitimacy for aggressive foreign interventions, including armed regime change in Iraq.
